title: Yesterday
blurb: Talk about what happened, from this morning to last weekend.

exercises.prompt: I was here two days ago

tip.title: Start with a time word
tip.body: Put a time word first to talk about the past. Ayer comí arroz means yesterday I ate rice. Hace dos días means two days ago.

exercises.prompt: What does "el fin de semana pasado" mean?
How do you say "an hour ago"?
Last week I worked a lot

tip.title: Past of -ar verbs
tip.body: Drop -ar and add -é for I, -aste for you and -ó for he or she. Hablé, hablaste, habló. The accent matters: hablo is now, habló is past.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday I bought bread and cheese

tip.title: Past of -er and -ir verbs
tip.body: Drop -er or -ir and add -í for I, -iste for you and -ió for he or she. Comí, comiste, comió. Both verb types use the same endings.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "he or she did"?
Yesterday I had a lot of work

tip.title: Learn these as they are
tip.body: Some very common verbs have their own past forms. Fui al mercado (I went to the market). Hice la cena (I made dinner).

tip.title: Ask about someone's day
tip.body: Use the tú form to ask: ¿Qué hiciste ayer? means what did you do yesterday. For how things were, learn chunks like hacía calor and estaba cansado.
